source.documentTitle: General Retail Industry Award 2020 [MA000004], Fair Work Commission consolidated modern award

notes: Adult employees (21 years or over) only; junior rates (cl. 17.2) are not modelled.
Non-shiftworkers only; Part 6 shiftwork rates (cl. 25) are not modelled.
Ordinary hours within the standard span of hours in cl. 15.1 Table 2 only; the cl. 15.2 exceptions (newsagencies, video shops, extended trading to 11 pm) are not modelled.
Overtime, public holidays, minimum engagement top-ups and the cl. 16.6 break-between-work-periods rate are detected and returned as REVIEW_REQUIRED, never calculated.
Allowances (cl. 19) and leave are outside scope.

rateRules.disabledReason: Public holiday dates differ by state and territory and substitution rules apply (cl. 32). WageGuard has no verified public holiday calendar, and cl. 22.2 allows an alternative arrangement by agreement, so hours on a declared public holiday are returned as REVIEW_REQUIRED.

CASUAL.description: Minimum daily engagement of a casual employee (1.5 hours only in the school-student circumstances of cl. 11.3).

sources.excerpt: The minimum daily engagement of a casual employee is 3 hours, or 1.5 hours’ in the circumstances set out in clause 11.3.

PART_TIME.description: Minimum daily engagement of a part-time employee.

sources.excerpt: The minimum daily engagement for a part-time employee is 3 consecutive hours.

maxOrdinaryPerDay.description: Maximum ordinary hours per day (up to 11 on one day per week by roster under cl. 15.5).

sources.excerpt: Subject to clause 15.5, the maximum number of ordinary hours that can be worked on any day is 9.
An employer may roster an employee to work up to 11 ordinary hours on one day per week.

casualWeeklyOrdinary.description: Casual overtime threshold: hours in excess of 38 ordinary hours per week (or averaged over a roster cycle).

sources.excerpt: Casual employee | Overtime is payable for hours worked: (i) in excess of 38 ordinary hours per week or, if the casual employee works in accordance with a roster, in excess of 38 ordinary hours per week averaged over the course of the roster cycle; or (ii) outside the span of ordinary hours (excluding shiftwork), subject to clause 15.2; or (iii) in excess of 11 hours on one day of the week and in excess of 9 hours on any other day of the week.

minimumBreakBetweenWorkDays.description: Minimum break between finishing work on one day and starting on the next (10 hours by agreement under cl. 16.6(d)).

sources.excerpt: An employee must have a minimum break of 12 hours between when the employee finishes work on one day and starts work on the next.

If an employee starts work again without having had 12 hours off work, the employer must pay the employee for each hour worked at the rate of 200% of the employee’s minimum hourly rate until the employee has a break of 12 consecutive hours.

mealBreakRequiredAfter.description: An employer cannot require more than 5 hours of work without a meal break. Informational: it does not change the calculated pay.

sources.excerpt: An employer cannot require an employee: ... (c) to work more than 5 hours without taking a meal break.

roundingPolicy.rationale: The award does not prescribe a rounding method. Rounding each hourly rate to cents half-up reproduces every Level 1 dollar rate published in Schedule B (B.1.1, B.2.1). Each pay line (rate × hours for one rule over the pay period) is then rounded once to cents, half-up. Employers may round at other stages, so reconciliation applies an explicit rounding tolerance.
